{"id":"425f4ff6-42ff-41ce-80c8-9a1989ce6a77","object":"chat.completion","created":1786997976,"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Both init variants fail identically, so the init fields aren't the cause. Let me test the registry's own `validated-fetch-query` example verbatim to see whether it discharges `fault_covered`.","reasoning_content":"Both variants fail fault_covered, even without method/headers. So the issue isn't the init fields. The example itself might be illustrative but not verified, OR there's something about the fetch call that requires more handling.

The suggestion: "add an explicit failure path for every critical I/O call site."

Hmm. The fetch call has a failure path via `!upstream.ok` → 502. But maybe the failure path must be attached differently, or the fetch response `ok` check isn't recognized, or there are TWO call sites: `fetch(...)` and `upstream.json()`.

Wait — maybe the pattern requires checking `upstream.ok` via a different idiom, or maybe the fetch module requires the `ok` check right after, which I do.

Let me check the properties: `fault_covered: false`. Let me get the pi_repair_plan for fault handling? The repair plan tool supports "missing fallback Response" as a v1 case. Actually let me look at what zts_expert_canonicalize says, or better, check if there's an example that verifies with fault_covered.

Let me check the example_registry. The full meta didn't include examples beyond the ones shown... Actually it did include `examples` (feature examples) and `module_examples`. The validated-fetch-query module_example claims fault_covered in the capsule.

Hmm, but maybe the module example is just documentation. Let me verify with zts_expert_verify_paths... file doesn't exist.

Alternative: use pi_repair_plan on a temp approach. But pi_repair_plan needs the file to exist on disk? It takes a path. The path handler.ts doesn't exist. Hmm.

Wait — but maybe I can create the file first? No, the only writer is propose_change_set and it vetoes. But zts_expert_review_patch works on content in memory. And zts_expert_prove_patch takes before/after.

Let me think about what makes fault_covered pass. The verifier is "path-enumeration". Perhaps the fetch call is considered to have TWO failure modes: `ok: false` and also... hmm.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the fetch signature: `fetch(url, init?)` returns `{ ok: boolean; status: number; ...; json: () => unknown; text: () => string }`. Perhaps the fault analysis treats `upstream.json()` as a faulting call (body parse can fail) and requires a failure path for it too. But in the example they call json() directly...

Let me test: handle both `!upstream.ok` and json parse failure. But how do you detect json() failure? json() returns unknown, not Result. Hmm.

Alternatively, maybe the fault analysis wants the failure path BEFORE any use: i.e., every critical I/O call site needs an explicit failure path, and the fetch failure path must be reached before `upstream.json()` is called. I do that.

Hmm, let me look at this from a different angle: maybe fault_covered for fetch requires `fetchWithRetry`? No...

Or maybe the issue is the URL: "https://api.example.com" — example.com might be flagged? No, that'd be a different error.

Let me try zts_expert_canonicalize on a draft to see candidates? That works on a handler file... needs file existence too probably.

Let me try zts_expert_prove_patch: classify before/after handler contract pair — needs before and after content. Not directly helpful.

Better approach: check the example_registry hash — maybe there are more examples in the full meta I didn't see. The meta output had "examples" (the feature list) and "module_examples" (2 entries). That's all.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the validated-fetch-query example. Its Proof claims include "fault_covered". But is that example actually verified by the compiler, or is it documentation? The module_examples are part of the registry with hashes. Let me test the EXACT example source (with validate) via review_patch to see if it passes. If it passes, I can diff. If it fails fault_covered too, then the example is aspirational documentation and I need a different shape.

Let me run the exact example through review_patch.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_HiQRkonpPpxahrGugkrb4121","type":"function","function":{"name":"zts_expert_review_patch","arguments":"{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { fetch } from \"zttp:fetch\";\nimport { schemaCompile, validateObject } from \"zttp:validate\";\n\nschemaCompile(\"cityQuery\", JSON.stringify({\n  type: \"object\",\n  required: [\"city\"],\n  properties: {\n    city: { type: \"string\", minLength: 1, maxLength: 64 }\n  }\n}));\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): Proof<Response,\n  | \"deterministic\"\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"fault_covered\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"no_secret_leakage\"\n  | \"no_credential_leakage\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n> {\n  const checked = validateObject(\"cityQuery\", { city: req.query[\"city\"] });\n  if (!checked.ok) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing or invalid city query parameter\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  const upstream = fetch(\"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast\", {\n    query: { city: checked.value[\"city\"] },\n    maxResponseBytes: 65536\n  });\n  if (!upstream.ok) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"weather service unavailable\" }, { status: 502 });\n  }\n  return Response.json(upstream.json());\n}\n"}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":25675,"completion_tokens":1353,"total_tokens":27028,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":25344},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":923},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":25344,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":331},"system_fingerprint":"a26a7955944dc5c60445bff77fac9c8e"}
